implementation_revision.semantics: WELL-131 reuses the certified fixed TB-001 proof unchanged in scope. The shared Chromium driver adds an ordinary entry mode and exact-text locale assertions; isolated production exclusion additionally checks the normal entry/content runtime flags. This record grants no new certification or release authority. WELL-134 adds a separately tested ordinary sign-in browser mode without changing the fixed TB-001 inventory. The stale-session browser check now verifies the approved confirmed-logout page rather than an empty 204 response. Isolated production exclusion additionally checks SignInCopy and both sign-in fixture flags. Shared browser failure diagnostics expose only existing allowlisted codes. No TB-001 certification or release is granted by this refresh. WELL-112 reconciles the stronger current-main scanner scenario and adds the self-hosted-font CSP assertion in its existing shared helper. Scenario owner-state checks and the fixed TB-001 inventory remain unchanged. Source/hash refresh is not a fresh TB-001 certification. WELL-114 changes test observations only: fixture queries filter before hydration, registration inputs are unique, and global Session/token maintenance proofs use rollback to preserve retained data. Business ownership and lifecycle are unchanged. Source-linked proof and refreshed hashes do not certify runtime completion, merge or resulting main. WELL-136 refreshes shared source references after independent semantic review; this mapped capability remains unchanged. The ordinary_reset Chromium mode is separate from the fixed TB-001 inventory and grants no certification. Shared P805 TEST guardian now also restores the ordinary-entry flag after normal completion or owner death; mapped business behavior is unchanged. WELL-153 coordinates registered TEST restart workers with P805 cleanup; no business lifecycle or Domain authority changed. WELL-153 now owns fixture admission before any global snapshot through safe scoped cleanup, restoration and release. VM-local quarantine retains exact synthetic targets across guardian failure; explicit reconciliation verifies registered workers and recorded OS process groups before retrying cleanup. No production Domain semantics changed. WELL-153 correlates each sequential TEST external-launch reservation. Proven pre-open validation or missing/non-executable launcher failure settles only its matching reservation; post-open uncertainty retains admission and reports unconfirmed cleanup. Production business behavior is unchanged. WELL-156 refreshes locators in shared source files. The new ordinary primary-email-change routes and context do not change this capability contract. The WELL-156 correction refreshes its shared source locators. WELL-146 scopes the held-email proof to DeliveryAttempt inserts issued by the synchronous TEST fixture. Returned UUIDs locate durable rows before teardown, including attempts under a foreign parent. A successful insert without an attributable UUID fails the observation. WELL-143 extends shared TEST creation ownership to MessageIntent and Session identifiers. Magic request observations and full-row Token/Session fingerprints exclude independent fixtures while retaining unexpected owned consequences. Maintenance proof separately checks foreign expired rows are restored after actual global maintenance rollback. P815 retains reset operation and account identifiers before JTI-based delivery. Production lifecycle and fixed proof inventory are unchanged; this evidence does not clear the unresolved P809 canonical failure. WELL-86 scopes interrupted Session issuance rollback to creation-owned full-row Token/Session fingerprints and retains failed assertion labels with boolean matches before raising. Permanent independent-owner and unexpected-owned-consequence tests preserve all existing guards and foreign rows. Backend absence is observed separately; no wait or retry is added. This repairs a demonstrated false-inclusion mechanism, without claiming attribution of historical intermittent failures or canonical success. The reconciled candidate keeps the WELL-148 active/quarantined lease and WELL-146 observer. The independent worker shares the lease environment but has a separate checkout and observation scope. Fallback cleanup retains only that worker’s explicit synthetic operations, emails and projection key. P809 proof remains separately attributed to WELL-86.

request_flow.summary: The canonical entrypoint invokes the unchanged Runner CLI. Catalog assembles nine mandatory business families plus separate browser_spine coverage.

The standalone canonical command independently binds all 133 case/invariant identities and the 74 P8-19 owner module/function/arity targets to the static TB-001-linked inventory. It compares the actual emitted boundary, cut, race and expected claim for each added case. Any declaration or claim mismatch leaves the affected family partial; Runner rejects it before any canonical callback executes. Inventory changes require an explicit independent review diff.

FullCatalog executes required callbacks in fixed order and stops after an unsatisfied invariant. Shared upstream scenarios retain their assertions. The P8-19 ledger records one aggregate owner_assertions marker only after the independently pinned named owner scenario returns normally. The marker does not enumerate each underlying ExUnit assertion; scenario implementation changes still require exact-source review.

The browser journey registers, resends, receives the test provider message, explicitly verifies, logs in and reloads protected access in one Chromium context. Endpoint observations prove verification did not create a Session.
Result validates source/runtime/dependency/TEST metadata, required cases/assertions and cleanup, then publishes without overwriting an existing path.

side_effects: Records the named invariant, cut/race metadata and bounded observations.

security_invariants.summary: Proof controls compile only under TEST. The broken-invariant subprocess recompiles a proof callback, then calls the same canonical Runner; ordinary full-proof CLI gains no override.
Evidence contains only fixed identities and bounded observations. Provider message bodies and bearer values remain transient in the synthetic browser/provider flow.
Fixture guardians restore browser flags and secret-bearing in-memory fixture configuration after normal completion or owner death.

Passive scanner checks snapshot full persisted Account, Token, Session, DeviceAssurance and RecoveryCase attributes for the fixture owner before the initial GET and after subsequent passive requests. Recovery neutrality compares all response headers, cookie attributes and session effects across known, unknown, invalid and source-unavailable outcomes; only request IDs, CSRF values and the encrypted anonymous-session cookie vary.

concurrency.summary: Upstream callbacks retain separate PostgreSQL connections, transaction identifiers and observed row-lock contention. New mappings reuse those routines, including both Privacy/Identity commit orders.

idempotency_retry.summary: Retries, replay, supersession and reconciliation remain existing owner semantics exercised by mapped scenarios. A proof rerun receives a new output path and never changes an earlier report.

failure_recovery.summary: Missing or partial coverage, callback failure, absent assertions, timeout, cleanup failure or incomplete/changing source metadata prevents PASS.
Existing fresh BEAM probes reconstruct Communications, recovery, Session, reconciliation and Privacy state from PostgreSQL. The integration adds no recovery authority.

The TEST guardian admits one correlated outstanding launch. It records the Port before OS identity lookup and completes the matching reservation after transfer. Proven no-child failures settle that reservation; an interrupted launch without recorded identity remains quarantined and rejects later launches. An interrupted transfer with a recorded target can reconcile only after existing worker, Port and OS-group checks pass.

No report commit after final capture without rerunning the canonical proof at the resulting head. No Phase-8 certification, WELL-21 completion or Phase-9 authorization is conferred.

proof_limitations: This source map is descriptive, not Product/Architecture/Domain or Plane authority.
No new migration, Resource, service, dependency or business write was added. The persistence entry identifies a reused constraint, not an exhaustive owner schema.
Final proof artifacts remain outside the checkout and must name the exact final PR head. Review actual artifacts and hosted CI independently.
The current Privacy purpose is a synthetic development/test proof, not a production consent requirement.
Full applicable local gates, OCR, exact-head CI and independent Master Gate review remain separate obligations. This map does not assert those results.

The static identity, owner callback-target and mandatory-claim inventory is linked to TB-001 sections 7-8. It remains separate from executable declarations and creates no business or certification authority. Fresh independent Master Gate review must assess semantic completeness and scenario source. The aggregate ledger marker does not enumerate underlying assertions or protect against arbitrary edits inside an owner scenario. Browser verification_form records the observed CSRF form; owning Account/Session/protected-access assertions determine success.

Isolated production exclusion additionally checks SignInCopy and both sign-in fixture flags. Shared browser failure diagnostics expose only existing allowlisted codes. No TB-001 certification or release is granted by this refresh.

WELL-112 source-reference refresh records the reconciled implementation, not a full-suite or integration pass. Current-base Content eligibility failures remain recorded under WELL-138 and WELL-136; canonical/deep, OCR, exact-head CI and independent certification remain separate obligations.

WELL-114 source checkpoint 145c2be adds fixture-isolation regression coverage and assertion-preserving test corrections. See docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-16-retained-fixture-observations.md for observed commands, test limits and current resource handling. Full applicable gates, OCR, exact-head CI and independent post-merge certification remain required. The original all-job privacy secret scan remains intentionally broad to detect incorrectly addressed leakage. The seven-file focused run passed 111/111, seed 985650. Canonical on clean 96a8455 passed 831/831, seed 813027, in 547.2 seconds under a command-scoped lock, after preserving and diagnosing a five-failure overlapping attempt and a same-seed 47/47 targeted pass. The focused plan records exact commands, fingerprints and limits. OCR, exact-final-head hosted CI and independent resulting-main certification remain separate requirements. Global maintenance tests use native Ecto sandbox checkout/checkin with signature restoration, rather than an outer Repo transaction that can be aborted by expected Ash denials.

Current-base WELL-114 proof: clean 9f4b8fd1975e0b1f67b12463e01156529ce7d57b incorporates main 2736a9c6925c8c126cbba007f404b2e38ec2080d with identical executable correction. Canonical passed 831/831, seed 813027, in 508.2 seconds; content compatibility passed 34/34 and routing/knowledge/smoke checks passed 71/71. Private per-row digest multisets preserve all preexisting rows across 15 tables, including membership in growing nonce and PMR sets, with no unexpected additions. DeliveryAttempt baseline was empty; permanent synthetic own/foreign coverage is separate. The focused plan records exact commands, hashes, observed counts, review limits and lost historical raw logs. Fresh OCR, final-head CI and independent integration/resulting-main certification remain separate requirements.

WELL-112 incorporates independently integrated WELL-114 from main f72cf637453408896a5037dcb2f8d37f0d29e3af. Earlier proof notes describe their historical checkpoints; new complete branch gates, OCR and independent review remain required. The floating-label variant is opt-in and does not migrate registration or change owner lifecycles.

WELL-153 fixture ownership and retained targets are local to the running TEST BEAM. They survive guardian failure, not termination of the whole VM. External evidence is limited to recorded Linux process groups from the controlled restart launcher. Missing launch identity or uncertain process state remains fail-closed; reconciliation has no assertion-based or force-release override. This is not deployed recovery certification.
